step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts Nielsen Marketing Cloud's DataOut system, which processes and uploads segmentation data to over 100 ad networks. External files arrive from a file source into an input S3 bucket, while file metadata is sent through an SQS queue to an ingestion Lambda that writes to an RDS PostgreSQL database. An EMR Work Manager Lambda reads metadata from RDS to trigger a Spark EMR cluster, which reads from the input S3 bucket, formats the data, writes transformed files to a second S3 bucket, and reports status back to RDS. A Fan-out Work Manager Lambda then reads metadata from RDS and invokes concurrent Uploader Lambdas (which scale up to thousands) to fetch formatted files from S3 and push them to external Ad Networks (ThirdParty). To prevent database connection limits, status results from the Uploader Lambdas are sent to a buffer SQS queue, which a Batch Writer Lambda reads to update RDS in batches.

graph.name: Nielsen Marketing Cloud DataOut Architecture
graph.notes: Handles 250 billion events per day using EMR and serverless Lambda functions, with buffer SQS queues for rate-limiting RDS updates.
